Escalation: elapsed-keyed beats and tiers.** *Rule.* Escalation is keyed to the **escalation clock** `esc_ticks`, published as `tell_elapsed` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(user ruling OQ-AT-25, Option A)*: it is 0 on the TELL-entry run and then advances by 6 on every run whose integrated `L' ≥ theta_HOLD` and stays where it is on every run under the line (the same comparison that counts `below_hold_runs`, AT-10). It is **never** keyed to progress through `tell_len`: a progress-keyed cadence peaks exactly at the breach and leaks the end, whereas keyed to the player's own behaviour a 600-tick and an 1800-tick tell are identical for as long as the clock runs (the dread of not knowing), and nothing the clock carries depends on `tell_len` or `breach_due_T`. A player who stays loud sees the clock equal real elapsed time (`T − tell_start_T`) and the schedule below is the old elapsed-keyed one exactly; a player who goes under the hold line freezes the beat interval and the tier where they are, because the signal is earned: complying never makes the tell worse, and the escalation resumes only if the level climbs back to the line. The clock never runs backwards, so `tier` never falls inside an epoch. Beats keep publishing in real time at the frozen interval until the abort or the due run; only the interval and the tier freeze. Real elapsed time stays derivable as `T − phase_enter_T` and is not a hidden quantity. One SIM counter, `tell_beat`, drives **both** senses: each increment is one audio beat and one visual filament-resolve event in every lit region. Beat 0 is published in the TELL-entry run, so audio is first and the presenter may render no filament for an epoch before beat 0 exists (the art bible's rule that every tell has an audio component starting no later than its visual, HR-9). The beat interval shrinks from `BEAT_START_TICKS` (150) to `BEAT_END_TICKS` (45) over `BEAT_RAMP_TICKS` (1800) of the escalation clock, with jitter of ±`BEAT_JITTER_TICKS` (8) from a **pure integer hash** of `(tell_epoch, k, HASH_SEED)`, never from `rng_derive`, and each gap at least `BEAT_MIN_GAP_TICKS` (30). The schedule is built from nominal offsets, so run quantisation (a beat may publish up to five ticks late) never accumulates. `tier = 0` outside TELL and `1 + (e ≥ 600) + (e ≥ 1200)` inside, with `e = esc_ticks` (the whole floor window is tier 1 whatever the player does, because `esc_ticks` never exceeds real elapsed time), which is Lighting's tier-1 recipe (registry `gutter_recipe`: tier 1 480/960 frames, tier 2 from `TIER2_TICKS` 300/600, tier 3 from `TIER3_TICKS` 180/360, placeholders). Filament density in a lit region is a function of `tell_beat` (AV-7), which follows this schedule. **Two-channel criterion.** (auto, headless) every legal `(tell_len, seed)` and every legal level trajectory (including a clock frozen from the first run) publishes at least `MIN_BEATS_IN_FLOOR` (4) beats in `[tell_start_T, tell_start_T + TELL_MIN_TICKS)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; (manual, screenshot plus audio capture) the presenter renders each beat in both senses; the audio channel is sufficient alone, and the visual channel is sufficient alone while an eligible emitter is lit (ART:954) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The lamp gutter is an optional **third** channel: Lighting's tier-1 spacing (480/960 frames) can give zero dips inside the 600-tick floor window (C2), so the contract does not lean on it; the shorter tier-2/3 spacing asked for in OQ-AT-7 now exists in the registry `gutter_recipe` as placeholder bounds. Attention publishes *facts*; Adaptive Audio & Tells owns every sound, mix and cue name (its requests are in Visual/Audio Requirements and Interactions as must-repeat). **Final-gap beat suppression is dropped (CQ-5, closed):** `BEAT_MIN_GAP_TICKS` constrains consecutive beats only, with no beat-to-breach gap, so the worst case for an organic tell in the floor window is five beats (offsets 0, 158, 307, 448, 580) against `MIN_BEATS_IN_FLOOR` 4, and the universal bound over every level trajectory (the clock frozen from the first run) is exactly four (0, 158, 316, 474; F-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; `BEAT_START_TICKS` 135 is recorded only as the fallback if the suppression ever returns. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), OQ-AT-25: escalation freezes while `L < theta_HOLD` (behaviour-keyed, Option A; the creative-director's call under coordination rule 3).** It replaces the elapsed-keyed text above, keeps the end unreadable (the clock keys on the player's own restraint, never on `tell_len`), changes AT-9, F-12, F-13, the persisted fields and the Audio tier layering (Adaptive Audio's contrary recommendation to reject freezing, OQ-AA-34, is superseded), and redoes the F-12 floor proof. The Feel AC AC-AT-125 still measures the share of first-time testers who stay still and reopens the ruling if it fails *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
200	*Criterion.* AC-AT-20 to AC-AT-24, AC-AT-47, AC-AT-127 (the freeze), AC-AT-128 (the floor under any trajectory). *Pillar.* P2. *Decided by:* R11; ART:954, :980; user ruling OQ-AT-25.
201	
202	**AT-10. Restraint aborts a tell.** *Rule.* During TELL, after each run's integration: if `L < theta_HOLD` then `below_hold_runs += 1`, else it resets to 0. The tell **aborts to CALM** when `below_hold_runs × 6 ≥ ABORT_HOLD_TICKS` (placeholder 120, run-quantised; the first run under the line counts as run 1), **or** at the first run with `T ≥ breach_due_T` if `L < theta_HOLD` at that run, **or** at that same run if the departure void holds (`locus_vacated`, AT-22; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*). If both are true on the same run the abort wins (one transition). An abort deposits no STRESS, switches no beacon, sets `tell_outcome = ABORTED`, freezes `tell_beat`, leaves `L` unchanged (a knob `ABORT_RELIEF_PM` defaulting to 1000, which means "no relief" and means the abort is unchanged from the ruled behaviour, lets a tuner cap the level at an abort if playtests show chained-abort fatigue) and sets `rearm_until_T = T + TELL_REARM_TICKS` (placeholder 600). **The rearm keys on the item, not on the pickup** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*: while a TELL runs, Attention records in `tell_carry_items` (persisted, AT-1) the `carry_ref` of every seat whose `BURDEN` push it drained (an ordered read of `controller.state`, the same read as `loco_state`, AT-31); after an abort the set is kept until `rearm_until_T`. On any CALM run before `rearm_until_T` that drains a `BURDEN` push from a seat whose `carry_ref` is in the set, `rearm_until_T` is set to that run's `T`, so dropping the cargo to abort and taking the same item up again grants no fresh `TELL_REARM_TICKS` immunity: the next crossing opens a tell at once. A different item leaves the rearm in place. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* The test is the push, not the pickup: any CALM run before `rearm_until_T` that drains a `BURDEN` push from a seat whose `carry_ref` is in the set ends the rearm, whether the seat re-took the item or never put it down (a continuous hold). By the location gate of AT-3 the push is not drained `IN_POD` or aboard the home body, so a hauler who hops with the item is not charged here: the void sets `rearm_until_T = T_d + TELL_REARM_TICKS` (`T_d` the due run) and it holds through the pod leg and the home carry. The cancel can fire after a hop only if the seat is back aboard a non-home body still holding the item before `rearm_until_T`: that takes a round trip, 2 × (`HOP_LEG_TICKS` 900 + `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` 45) = 1,890 ticks from the hop, against a rearm that ends d + 600 ticks after the hop (d = ticks of the tell still to run at the hop), so it is reachable only when d > 1,890 − 600 = 1,290 (a hop in the first 510 ticks of an 1,800-tick tell); otherwise the rearm is whole. The narrower rule, that only a re-take cancels, is not adopted (creative-director lean). The set is cleared at TELL entry (and refilled during the tell), at BREACH entry (a breached tell sets no rearm) and when the rearm ends. A player who keeps being loud through the tell forfeits the abort; that is intended ("we chose to be loud"). Restraint always costs the partial (Formulas F-15b), and that price is deliberate *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; it is balanced by a breach that has teeth (AT-11), so neither choice dominates. `tell_remaining` published to Save/Load is the time to `breach_due_T`: the conservative direction, because an abort only ends the block early. Two invariants, both lint: **(a) rearm against autosave:** `TELL_REARM_TICKS ≥ AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS` (cited), which guarantees an open soft-gate window between chained aborted tells even under STRICT mode. **(b) abortability at entry:** a player who enters TELL at the highest possible level (`L_CEIL`, AT-5) and then zeroes every player-controlled input (still, beam off, no verbs, any cargo set down) falls under `theta_HOLD` minus a margin `ATT_MARGIN` before `TELL_MIN_TICKS − 6` ticks elapse, at the ring's survivable-dark floor. In words: the tell is a window of agency even at its shortest. The play-level variant, which adds a reaction allowance and evaluates against the shortest draw a player can actually meet, is the registered formula `abortability_play` (AT-8, CQ-4; Formulas F-15b).
203	*Criterion.* AC-AT-25, AC-AT-26, AC-AT-27, AC-AT-16, AC-AT-52. *Pillar.* P3 (restraint is real), P2 (a tell is a window of agency). *Decided by:* R10; Pillar 3 design test.
204	
205	#### Group E — The breach and its locus
206	
207	**AT-11. Breach entry actions (same run).** *Rule.* At the run that satisfies `T ≥ breach_due_T` with `L ≥ theta_HOLD`: `phase = BREACH`, `breach_enter_T = T`; record `locus_occupants_at_entry` = the set of living seats whose `actor_section` is in `locus_body` at this BREACH-entry run; M17 `deposit_trace(STRESS, s, magnitude = BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT)` for every section `s` of the locus body, in ascending `section_id`, at most `STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` (placeholder 8) per run, continuing on following runs (`stress_pending_cursor`) until the body is covered; and `set_beacon(on)` submitted as a `SYSTEM` command at T+1 (CR-9 path b). The magnitude is cited by registry name and never as a number; passing that constant as `magnitude` also makes the Graph's M17 clamp reading (`stress_pm = clamp(magnitude, 1000, 3000)`) and its D.9 / LS-25 reading (`stress_pm = BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT`) agree (C15, a Graph wording refresh). **Footprint cap:** `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` bounds honoured footprints per Graph run; Attention takes at most `STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` per run. **Attention has no first claim on the cap** (CP-C5): Horror's footprints arrive by **path (a)**: the published Class B mutators `deposit_trace` (M17) and `apply_suit_damage`, called from the `horror.step` hook, which is ordered `after` Attention (KRN Interactions row 9; Horror HE-28, C-HE-3), not as SYSTEM commands in P2; Horror submits no SYSTEM command at MVP. The Graph's "first `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` in arrival order within P2" (LSG:807) carries a P2 premise that path (a) does not satisfy, so Attention claims no first place in the cap. The guarantee is therefore a **Horror must-repeat**: its per-run footprint budget is at most `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP − STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN`. The registry unit of `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` (revised 2026-10-27) says per run across all callers and subjects (global), the first 16 by arrival applied in ascending subject id and the rest dropped and counted, which matches LSG:727 (C22). A STRESS deposit the cap drops is not lost for good: the next burst run re-arms it (AT-12; an edge case below). **Attention's MVP breach is STRESS plus the beacon plus the published phase.** RUPTURE and GOUGE are Horror's; this keeps Attention fully testable without Horror. **Stance (the breach is a consequence amplifier, stated so it is a decision):** STRESS multiplies *endogenous* damage only ("the breach rhythm makes the ship *fail* faster, not *leak* faster", LSG D.9), so a breach costs the crew what they had deferred; on a clean ship it would be nearly a non-event. **Why this is not left as a stance (gate ruling, CD-GDD-ALIGN, applied):** each choice is defensible alone, but a toothless breach on a clean ship together with an abort that always forfeits the partial (AT-10, Moment A) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* makes *commit* the dominant choice. Restraint would always cost the partial, riding it out would cost almost nothing, P3's "restraint and stealth are real strategies" would be empty, the "chaos" half of P2 would have no chaos, and players would learn to ignore tells. Two requirements follow, and neither is a mitigation to be traded away. **(1) Content requirement (a Derelict Authoring must-repeat).** Every body that can be a locus on MVP derelicts A and B is authored with at least one active overload or fatigue fault (on derelict A, a fault that wakes when its bus is served: option (b), OQ-AT-24), so a derelict breach always has something to amplify (AC-AT-58 is the seeded-fault scenario, AC-AT-117 the authoring check). This fits P5: the outer ring is kept unsafe by wear. A body the player has repaired clean is the player's earned result and not a content failure, and a home-ship locus carries whatever the crew has left unrepaired. **(2) Horror Entities' single MVP behaviour wired to BREACH is a BLOCKING dependency** (OQ-AT-9, AC-AT-77), no longer an ask: a breach brings the thing the crew fears, not only a faster-failing hull. `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT` is not raised to hide this. **Playtest tripwire:** the Moment-ordering guard (Player Fantasy, AC-AT-80) is named for exactly this failure: a 30-minute session with only breaches means commit has become dominant. **Re-evaluated against the designed Horror and Derelict Authoring** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the claim that STRESS alone leaves a derelict breach toothless was written before Horror existed. Horror now supplies crew-side teeth of its own: by HE-F16 a stationary seat in the locus body cannot be killed in a minimum-length breach (`BREACH_MIN_TICKS` 900 gives two REACH starts) but can be in any breach of at least 986 ticks and certainly in any of at least 1,156, and the REACH ladder (HE-F13, HE-F17) gives the breach a content beat. The breach therefore has two teeth: STRESS (ship-side, it amplifies deferred faults) and Horror's REACH (crew-side, it needs a seat that lingers); neither substitutes for the other, and a crew that leaves the body by pod is exposed to neither beyond the STRESS tail. Requirement (1) stays as the ship-side tooth. **Derelict A, option (b)** (creative-director recommendation; **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), OQ-AT-24: option (b)**, which preserves EM-24's count of 8 live faults; the dead-bus exemption (a) is not adopted) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: its pass condition is a Graph subject authored with a fault that *wakes when its bus is served* (`j_a_main`, a dead SHORT that becomes live once fed, with `pump_a` on its branch), which keeps Emitter State's count of exactly 8 live faults (EM-24) and adds no ninth fault. **Story-readiness gate:** a story that builds AT-11, the breach ACs or Derelict Authoring's locus lint is not ready until AC-AT-58's tolerance is fixed with the Graph owner (OQ-AT-6); OQ-AT-24 is answered (user ruling, option (b)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
208	*Criterion.* AC-AT-28, AC-AT-29, AC-AT-30, AC-AT-58 (seeded-fault scenario). *Pillar.* P2, P3. *Decided by:* R12; LSG:196, :525, :906.
209	
210	**AT-12. Breach duration and end.** *Rule.* During BREACH the level **keeps integrating** (the player's noise still matters), with `W_L[FAULT_GLOW] = W_L[BEACON] = 0` and the beacon's lamp watts never reaching the power terms (`bcn_main` is a LAMP node, so it sits inside `lamps_lit_w`, AT-4; the alarm cannot hold the level above `theta_HOLD` and delay the exit it is tested against) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. STRESS is re-armed in **bursts**: `STRESS_REFRESH_BURST_RUNS` (3) consecutive runs every `STRESS_REFRESH_RUNS` (placeholder 300) runs, under the lint `STRESS_REFRESH_RUNS + STRESS_REFRESH_BURST_RUNS < STRESS_HOLD_STEPS` (cited from LSG:907; registry `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS`). A burst tolerates one dropped deposit because a deposit is idempotent. BREACH ends at the first of: (i) `BREACH_MAX_TICKS` (placeholder 3600, the death-spiral guard); (ii) after `BREACH_MIN_TICKS` (placeholder 900), `L < theta_HOLD` for `CLEAR_HOLD_TICKS` (placeholder 300, run-quantised); (iii) pod-hop departure: the last living occupant recorded at BREACH entry (`locus_occupants_at_entry`) leaving a locus body that is not the home-ship (AT-22); (iv) **ADDITION X10 (APPROVED at the CD-GDD-ALIGN gate: the combat anti-pillar explicitly permits decoys, and the lit derelict pays in STRESS on its own hardware; CR-LURE stays a playtest watch item with `LOCUS_OCC_PREF_PM` as the lever):** if at BREACH entry the locus body is not the home-ship and `locus_occupants_at_entry` is empty (it holds no living player), at `BREACH_MIN_TICKS` (the retreat the departure clause models has already happened) (reachable at MVP only through a derelict that Web Map keeps loaded while berthed, WM-21 and WM-24, after the player has left it; a *departed* unberthed derelict goes dormant at once under LS-17's default, which Web Map adopts, so that form is fixture-only *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*). **Breach length is Attention's, not `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS`.** STRESS lapses on the Graph's own hold after the last deposit and may outlast SUBSIDING: "a long tell, a spreading wrongness, a short collapse, then silence" (LSG:986). No Attention surface shows that tail. **Must-repeat request to Adaptive Audio & Tells (R30):** `phase == CALM` is never mapped to an "all clear" cue, because the Graph's consequence sounds, not Attention, carry the ongoing wrongness; this is Audio's rule to repeat, not Attention's.
211	*Criterion.* AC-AT-31, AC-AT-32, AC-AT-33 (lint), AC-AT-34. *Pillar.* P2, P3. *Decided by:* R12.
212	
213	**AT-13. Subsiding and the refractory.** *Rule.* On SUBSIDING entry: `set_beacon(off)` is submitted; no further STRESS deposits are made; and the level is reset to a residual, not wiped: `L ← min(L, B + POST_PM × (theta − B) / 1000)` with `POST_PM` a placeholder of 400. SUBSIDING lasts `SUBSIDE_TICKS` (placeholder 1200) while integrating normally, then the machine returns to CALM with `refract_until_T = T + REFRACT_TICKS` (placeholder 1800) and `tell_outcome = BREACHED`. During the refractory no TELL may begin, but the level keeps integrating, so **the refractory is not free safe time**: a player still loud at its end tips straight into a new tell (bounded by `L_CEIL`). The refractory is a published, state-gated valley, not a hidden scheduler. `phase` changes only inside `attention.step`; `post_restore` changes no phase and submits nothing (AT-27), so no reader can observe a half state; CALM → BREACH, TELL → SUBSIDING and BREACH → TELL do not exist. The phase table, guards and who may cause each transition are in States and Transitions.
214	*Criterion.* AC-AT-35, AC-AT-36, AC-AT-60 (table-driven transition test). *Pillar.* P2. *Decided by:* R13; LSG:986.
215	
216	**AT-14. Locus and locus body.** *Rule.* The **locus** is the section with the highest `ledger_mAU` at TELL entry; ties go to the lowest `section_id`. It is fixed for the epoch and falls back to the home-ship's lowest `section_id` only if the locus section is cut away or goes dormant *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* and no departure void applies: the fallback never converts an escape into a breach on the ship the player escaped to (AT-22, E-23). **During a TELL the dormancy fallback is suppressed from the first run at which `locus_vacated` holds** (a non-home locus body, `tell_occupants_at_entry` non-empty, no living seat in `locus_body`): the departure apply makes the derelict dormant many runs before `breach_due_T`, and without this the fallback would re-point the locus at the home ship in between and the due-run void would then never see the recorded body. The locus stays pinned to the departed body for the epoch (`locus_section_id` and `locus_body` remain valid ids; its ledger entry is dropped per AT-2, which is harmless because the locus is fixed), and the void resolves at the due run. The fallback is taken during a TELL only for a cut, a berth release, or a dormancy with a living seat still in the body. Attribution: a PlayerId source maps to the section containing the actor's foot origin through Ship Body's `actor_section(actor_id)` (BDY-29, Section lookup for Suit; sibling in flight); an object or emitter source maps to `section_of` or the emitter's `section_id`; light and power map to their own section. The **locus body** is `sections_of(body_of(locus))` (Layout reads, LY state inventory and Body row), recorded at TELL entry as `locus_body`. STRESS covers the whole locus body: welded sections share the breach, so a welded derelict is not a safe harbour. An optional knob `LOCUS_OCC_PREF_PM` (default 1000 = "leader only", conforming) lets a tuner prefer a section holding a living player if playtests show an unattended, powered derelict absorbing most breaches. Layout's pathing asks (`room_surface`, `floor_tile_at`, `room_adjacency`, LY Interactions row for Attention / Horror) are Horror's; Attention takes only the membership reads.
217	*Criterion.* AC-AT-37, AC-AT-59 (decoy knob default reproduces the rule). *Pillar.* P3. *Decided by:* R14.
218	
219	#### Group F — The contract, the view, the truth channel
220	
221	**AT-15. The tell-window contract: one predicate for all web-originated harm.** *Rule.* `exogenous_permitted(section) = phase ∈ {BREACH, SUBSIDING} AND section ∈ locus_body`. Every web-originated exogenous call (M17 RUPTURE, GOUGE and STRESS; environmental M18 `apply_damage(..., EXOGENOUS)`) must satisfy it. A `TellAudit` ledger (a DIAGNOSTIC subscriber and a **test fixture first**, written before Horror and Audio exist) records each such call as `(tick, caller, kind, section, tell_epoch, phase)`; it also records every AT-14 fallback as `LOCUS_FALLBACK(epoch, old_body, new_body, tick)`, and the replay evaluates `section_e` against the body in force at `t_e`; the replay asserts, for every harm event `e`, that some epoch `k` satisfies `tell_start_k + tell_len_k ≤ t_e < subside_end_k` with `tell_len_k ≥ TELL_MIN_TICKS` and `section_e ∈ locus_body_k` (registry formula `tell_window_contract`). **Scope (R15, provisional):** TellAudit also records every lethal act by a horror on a crew body, because the Pillar 2 promise ("every breach is preceded by a 10–30 second tell") is a promise to the *player*, not to the hull; a lethal act outside a told breach is exactly the ambush Pillar 2 forbids, and Horror's stalk is additive, never a substitute. **Horror Entities must REPEAT this rule or surface a CONFLICT.** "Perceivable" is defined relative to **every living player**, not to the locus: the tell must be audible to all of them through the non-positional structure-borne bed, whose existence and listener scope are contractual (its dB margin is Audio's). The bed is what makes a tell on an unoccupied lit derelict fair. Player-originated exogenous acts (cut, vent) never need the tell (LSG:144: agency); the Graph's endogenous gate (`W_MIN_WARNING_S`) is not how this contract is enforced and neither replaces nor is replaced by it. **This rule discharges LSG:1063** ("every call site of M17 RUPTURE, GOUGE and STRESS and every environmental M18 `apply_damage(…, EXOGENOUS)` source is preceded by that system's own 10–30 s Pillar 2 tell, named in its GDD, and none relies on the Graph's gate for it").
222	*Criterion.* AC-AT-01 (first; discharges LSG:1063), AC-AT-01a, AC-AT-68 (the provisional crew-body scope). *Pillar.* P2. *Decided by:* R15; LSG:144, :1063.

## Detailed Design

### Core Rules

*Conventions.* Rules are named `AT-n`. Each states a **Rule**, a **Criterion** (acceptance-criterion ids `AC-AT-nn`, written in Acceptance Criteria; the tell-window ones are written first, as the index requires) and a **Pillar**. Citations name the counterpart document and section; line numbers (`LSG:144`, `EM:247`, `IA:276`, `SL:528`, `ART:741`) were verified against the files on disk on 2026-10-26 and are given for convenience. **Units.** A *run* is one execution of `attention.step` (6 ticks at `TICK_RATE`, the Graph's `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`); the level is stored in **mAU** (milli-attention-units, 64-bit integer); **1 AU is one walking tick of noise** (defined by the Controller-owned registry row `NOISE_PER_TICK`, cited, never restated with a number here). All durations are ticks. Every new number below is a `[PLACEHOLDER]`, tuned in `assets/data/attention/`; the ruling that fixed its form is named in parentheses. **Disk state at authoring (Glob of `design/gdd/`, 2026-10-26, re-run at the part 2 pass: 17 files including this one):** designed and read: Command & Simulation Layer, Life-Support Graph, Player Controller & Input, Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query, Suit & Equipment, Save/Load & Versioned Format, Interaction System, 2D Lighting & Occlusion, Item & Module Database, Failure & Trail, Ship Section & Layout Data Model, Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera. Two neighbours are on disk with status `In Design` and are **siblings in flight**, so they are cited by section id first and their line numbers drift (every `BDY:` and `DA-` line below is as of the 21:21 write and must be re-grepped): **Ship Body & Interior Physics** (`ship-body-and-interior-physics.md`) and **Derelict Authoring (Handmade Kits)** (`derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md`; DA-24: exactly one BEACON in the world, on `home_ship` in `spine_corridor`, `node_ref` = `bcn_main`, a dedicated LOAD node (`mod_lamp`, 20 W, DA-24; OQ-DA-9 closed 'no sharing'), lint `BEACON_COUNT` (ERROR, BOOT), none on derelicts A or B; DA-23: `fx_cryo_lamp` is an EMERGENCY fixture, self-powered (`node_ref` 0) and never modulated by Attention's tell). *(Superseded 2026-10-27 — design review: every file named in this paragraph now exists with status Designed, including Ship Body and Derelict Authoring, which were In Design when this was written. Their rows are no longer provisional as to existence; each *must repeat* clause is a contract to diff, not a status to tick. Line numbers in this document are advisory and drift: cite by section or rule id.)* No file existed for Horror Entities, Sanity & Hallucination Rules, Adaptive Audio & Tells, Web Map & Transit, Modular Ship Assembly, Perception Filter, Boarding & Salvage, HUD & Suit Layer, In-World Instruments, Chart Table or Debug Overlay at authoring: every contract with those was **provisional** and carries a *must repeat* clause.

#### Group A — Identity and scope

**AT-1. Block and hook identity.** *Rule.* One `SIM` block `attention.state` and one step hook `attention.step`. Both ids are new; the hook's `after` ids already exist, so an unknown id cannot fail boot.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| hook | `(hook_id attention.step, owner attention, divisor 6, offset 0, after [graph.propagate.power, emitter.place])` |
| why offset 0 | LS-8: a reader shares its writer's offset (LSG:104). The kernel's stagger example "Graph 0, Attention 2, Suit 4" (KRN Formulas, D.6 Output Range) is a refresh owed (C3); it is not edited here |

A lamp switch-off refused `TOO_SOON` waits at most `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS` (12 ticks, Emitter-owned) from the last toggle, which is inside `REACT_ALLOW_TICKS` (180) and so changes no lint.

Power *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the one formula is **F-4**; this rule states it in words only (it no longer carries a second, unscaled copy). Attention reads the Graph's `power_use(section_id)` exactly as LS-19 now defines it: `draw_w` is the section's total served load (lamps and inrush included), `lamps_lit_w` is the served watts of LOAD subtype LAMP (it includes the beacon's own node `bcn_main`), `delta_w_last5` is a *signed* five-run delta that **includes lamp watts** and reads 0 after a load, and `noisy_w` is the served watts of SCRUBBER, PUMP, HEATER and DOOR_MOTOR nodes. Lamps are light and must not be counted twice (EM-27), so Attention works on the **non-lamp draw** `nl_w = max(0, draw_w − lamps_lit_w)`: a steady term `W_P × nl_w` and a transient term `W_S × max(0, nl_w now − nl_w five runs ago)`. Because the Graph publishes no lamp-excluded delta, Attention keeps its own five-deep history of `nl_w` per loaded section (`nl_hist_w[section]`, persisted, AT-1), seeded flat with the current value whenever a section loads or wakes, so a section that wakes already drawing 2,500 W adds **0** transient input on its first run. The Graph's `delta_w_last5` and `noisy_w` are **not** read (`noisy_w` stays reserved at weight `W_N` 0). The beacon needs no special case: `bcn_main` is a LAMP node, so its draw and its switch-on step are inside `lamps_lit_w` and never reach `nl_w` (the earlier `beacon_w` and `beacon_step_w` subtractions are deleted). Carried in OQ-AT-6 and the cross-GDD notes. If `power_use` is absent, `I_power` is 0 for that section and one diagnostic is logged per process. The **Suit pushes nothing** (SE-31); **Assembly pushes nothing at MVP**, because Interaction already pushes LOUD at cut completion and a second push would double count; no `LOUD` is pushed at weld completion by anyone (Modular Ship Assembly T14 C5; IA-33). **Attention never reads Audio** (lint; the player's footsteps enter only as the Controller's pushed gait class).

#### Group C — The level, the baseline, the threshold

**AT-5. The integrator: one level, one memory constant (a rate detector).** *Rule.* Each run: the three channel inputs are summed (`I_run = I_noise + I_light + I_power`), a **ceiling decay** toward the baseline `B` is subtracted, and the result is clamped to `[B, L_CEIL]`. There is one memory, `TAU_ATT_TICKS` (placeholder 1800: a job split across `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` then retains about 72 percent). There is **no separate spike term**: the power inrush enters as ordinary input over its at most five steps, because a second memory would contradict Interaction's single `tau_att`. The ceiling decay reaches `B` *exactly* (the integer truncation stall of LSG:464 cannot occur). **A held salvage carry suspends the decay** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*: on a run that drained at least one `BURDEN` push (the persisted flag `pending_burden`, AT-1, F-1), `dec` is 0, so while any seat holds a salvage carry the level can only rise; the section ledger keeps its own decay (it only chooses the locus). Freezing with cargo is priced (user ruling X3), and the abortability lints are unchanged because every one of them assumes the cargo is set down (F-15b). Calibration placeholders: `ATT_THRESHOLD` (theta) 6000 AU, so continuous running with the beam on crosses theta in tens of seconds and continuous walking settles near 30 percent of theta; the derivation is in Formulas. A lint also bounds theta **from above** (F-5): a theta near the asymptote of the sustained verbs, about 8,000 AU, would make running or cutting unable to cause a tell *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
**ADDITION X1 (adopted by checkpoint ruling CQ-2; APPROVED at the CD-GDD-ALIGN gate): `L_CEIL`.** `L_CEIL = ATT_THRESHOLD × L_CEIL_PM / 1000`, placeholder `L_CEIL_PM` 1020. The ruled abortability invariant (AT-10 b) is stated for "the highest possible entry level, theta plus one run's input", but the entry level is not bounded by that: during the refractory and rearm windows the level keeps integrating and a runner can reach several times theta before the next legal tell, and one run's maximum input has no design bound (96 emitters alone are over 200 AU per run at weight 1000). Saturating the level at `L_CEIL` is the only way for the proof to exist, and it is what makes the abortability proof, and so P2's "window of agency", true at every entry level (the gate's reason for approving it). It changes nothing below theta.
**Stance (so no later pass "fixes" it): the level is a short-memory rate detector, not a session score.** With a memory of tens of seconds, a TELL means "you have been loud or lit at a high rate for roughly half a minute to a minute", never "you have done much in total". That makes causality local and legible (P3) and is why pacing comes from behaviour and not from drift. A longer `TAU_ATT_TICKS` is the only lever that makes a whole sortie matter, and it is capped from above by abortability (AT-10).
*Criterion.* AC-AT-11, AC-AT-12, AC-AT-13, AC-AT-14, AC-AT-57a to AC-AT-57g (calibration traces). *Pillar.* P3. *Decided by:* R4; IA:221 and :321 (one `tau_att`).

**AT-6. Baseline by depth.** *Rule.* `B = B_table[ring_B]`, where `ring_B` is the **maximum ring over sections that contain a living player** (a deterministic rule; "loudest player" is rejected as undefined). `ring_of(section_id)` is the registry formula `ring_of` (Web Map & Transit): the owning record's ring, a welded section resolving to the HOME ring, a parked pod to the ring of the record at `pod_at`, a pod mid-leg to the departure record's ring (equal to `held_ring`, AT-22); an absent or sub-1 ring resolves to 1, logged once per process. While a player is `IN_POD` the ring of the departure section is held (`held_ring`) until arrival. MVP ships ring 1 plus placeholder rows for rings 2 and 3 for tests; per-ring values belong to Depth Rings & Scarcity (Vertical Slice). A ring change that raises `B` above `L` lifts `L` to `B` at once; one that lowers `B` lets `L` decay toward the new floor. Two invariants are written as lint and automated criteria over the data: (i) `B_table` is non-decreasing with ring; (ii) the **survivable-dark floor**: at every ring, the dark steady level `x_dark` (the baseline plus everything the player cannot switch off, with the player still and the beam off) must satisfy **both** bounds. *The trivial steady bound* (R7 ii as ruled): `x_dark ≤ theta_HOLD − ATT_MARGIN`. *The binding bound* (F-15, AT-10 b): the decay from `L_CEIL` at that floor must reach `theta_HOLD − ATT_MARGIN` before `TELL_MIN_TICKS − 6` ticks elapse, which caps `x_dark` far below the trivial bound (about 1,253 AU at the placeholders, against 4,750 AU for the trivial one). **The unswitchable set** is named: (1) the cryo EMERGENCY lamp (`fx_cryo_lamp`, self-powered, DA-23), (2) `FAULT_GLOW` emitters (counted in CALM and TELL; a latent fault the player cannot extinguish), (3) `DARK_FLOOR_LOAD_W`, the home-ship's minimum survival load (O2, heat, reactor) with lamps off, through the power channel, and (4) the DOCK_STATUS glow of the berthed pod's dock room (X2: self-powered, `node_ref` 0 and switched by SYSTEM only, so the player cannot extinguish it; at most one is lit at a time because there is one pod; its output times reach is budgeted in F-16) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The lint re-runs whenever Assembly, Authoring or the Graph changes that set. This is what guarantees that restraint can always end a tell and that no depth makes a breach unavoidable. **Which abortability guarantee holds** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: two statements had been blurred. **(A) Abortable at the switches:** a player who zeroes every input, sets any cargo down, kills the lamp and opens the breaker (home dark, survival load only) falls under the line inside the floor length at every ring row (F-15, F-16); this is the **guaranteed** one and the data lint enforces it at every row (the open breaker is the lint's best-case posture, not a lever the player needs: in play it saves about 2 seconds that its inrush gives back on re-closing, and the abort share by reaction latency of F-25 shows what each posture buys *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*). **(B) Abortable anywhere:** the same player with the home ship left lit and not at the switches (the lit fixtures keep feeding the level) must still fall under the line within the **played** range (F-15b, row `x_dark_home_lit`); it holds at MVP ring 1 only, with thin slack (48 ticks on a clean ship, 24 with the two wake glows) and fails at the ring 2 and ring 3 test rows with the glows (-6 and -30 ticks), so those rows are flagged `SWITCHES`. Positive transients the player did not cause (an auto-reclose after a SCRAM, duty cycling, a STRESS-driven fault) are bounded by neither lint; the new row `autonomous_transient` adds the worst one (a 1,500 W cold start: 270 AU over five runs, landing at its worst moment) and shows that (B) does **not** survive it (-138 ticks at ring 1 with the glows) while (A) at the played range survives it at ring 1 (slack 30) and not at the ring-3 test row with the glows (-12). The creative-director's preference is (B) at ring 1 including the transient, met by retuning (the computed routes are `TELL_DRAW_LO` at least 1,038 or `HOLD_PM` about 850, each of which changes the felt tell or the cost of restraint and a registered value); that choice is OQ-AT-26, **default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20) (D49): neither retune is applied**, (A) abortable at the switches stays the guarantee and the `autonomous_transient` row stays boot-advisory (WARN), to be revisited after the AC-AT-57 harness exists. The X3 recalibration (F-26) adds only a player-controlled input (the cargo, set down with `drop`) and changes no input of F-15, F-15b or F-16, so it does not move this default *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
**Consequence stated honestly (risk RK-2):** at the ruled memory and hold band the invariant caps the deep-ring baseline at a small fraction of theta, so on the Attention axis P3's "Depth sets the baseline" and P5's "Deeper Is Richer" are almost inert; that is acceptable for a ring-1-only MVP and not beyond it. **Pillar-flagged Vertical Slice REQUIREMENT (gate ruling, CD-GDD-ALIGN; no longer a proposal):** a per-ring stimulus gain on the light and power channels only, never applied to noise (footsteps are the player's only noise readout and its scale must not change with depth), which Depth Rings & Scarcity must satisfy or surface as a CONFLICT. Vertical Slice acceptance criterion: AC-AT-119.
*Criterion.* AC-AT-15, AC-AT-16, AC-AT-64 (`abortability_play`). *Pillar.* P5, P3. *Decided by:* R7; IDX bullet 17 ("baseline set by depth"), Systems Enumeration row for Depth Rings.

**AT-7. One threshold, one hold band.** *Rule.* One threshold `theta = ATT_THRESHOLD`, identical for every ring at MVP, plus a hold band `theta_HOLD = theta × HOLD_PM / 1000` (placeholder `HOLD_PM` 800). TELL entry requires **all** of: phase CALM, `L ≥ theta`, `T ≥ refract_until_T`, and `T ≥ rearm_until_T` (the guards are inclusive, so entry exactly at a timer boundary is legal). Per-ring thresholds are a Vertical Slice addendum. **(Orchestrator ruling: R8's absolute definition of theta_HOLD stands.)** The game-designer's proposal GD-3 defines the hold line relative to the baseline instead (`B + HOLD_PM × (theta − B) / 1000`) because the absolute line lengthens the descent when `B` is large; the two are close at ring 1. The question is carried to Open Questions; it is moot while the baseline stays under the cap that AT-6 (ii) and AT-10 (b) impose, and the lint over every ring row is the guard.
*Criterion.* AC-AT-17. *Pillar.* P3. *Decided by:* R8; game concept ("MVP: one threshold").

#### Group D — The tell

**AT-8. The tell window: length and the floor (contract part 1).** *Rule.* At TELL entry, `tell_len = rng_int(TELL_DRAW_LO, TELL_DRAW_HI)` (inclusive), drawn with `rng_derive(world_seed, "attention.tell", counter_eff)`, where `counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE × restore_epoch` is **the kernel's one derivation for threat draws**, called and never re-derived here (Command & Simulation Layer owns it and `RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE`; Horror calls the same derivation) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)*, then `rng_counter` increments *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(user ruling D16: threat draws re-key per restore epoch)*. Two things stay exact: `rng_counter` is persisted and restored unchanged, and a `tell_len` already drawn is persisted with the block, so a restore taken during a TELL replays that tell's length and beats and cannot reroll it (no reroll oracle). What changes is the key of every draw made **after** a restore. `restore_epoch` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* is Save/Load's persisted u32, held in the per-slot side file `slot_epoch.bin` (each generation header keeps only a read-only copy, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA never change) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14)*: it starts at 0; a death-stub restore advances it by 1, and so does a Continue of any generation other than the newest non-demoted verified `QUIT` generation (after a kill, crash or fallback, in one process or after a fresh start); Save/Load makes each advance durable before it calls `request_restore`. A Continue of that newest `QUIT` generation carries it unchanged, so a Save & Quit then Continue replays the identical tell draws (quit buys no re-roll), while two death restores of one autosave give two new epochs. If the epoch write fails, the restore proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory and Save/Load logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` with `save_status = FAILED`; a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once, an exposure Save/Load lists and owns (R14). The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as `(T, world_seed, restore_epoch)`. It is never stored in `attention.state`, so the block's round trip stays idempotent, and **no fallback is needed**: the clock always carries an epoch (0 before the first restore). Determinism is defined given (save bytes, `restore_epoch`): the same pair replays identically, and tests pin the epoch. `RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE` is the kernel's fixed 2^20 (value unchanged; Attention keeps its own lint `rng_counter < RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE`); the Graph's physical failures and every other persisted counter replay exactly as before, because Pillars 1 and 5 want the scrubber that fails at minute four to fail at minute four. Attention's requirements on the supplied value (Save/Load and the kernel own the mechanism): it is constant between restores, it differs after each advancing restore (every death-stub restore; every Continue except one of the newest `QUIT` generation) and is unchanged by a Continue of the newest `QUIT` generation, and it is a function of the restore history alone (never of player input, a wall clock or a random source), so the player cannot choose it and quit and death offer no way to read or pick a length beforehand (OQ-37). The beat jitter keeps its pure hash of `(tell_epoch, k, HASH_SEED)`: ±`BEAT_JITTER_TICKS` ticks cannot carry an ambush. `TELL_MIN_TICKS` is **derived, not a knob**: `ticks_for_seconds(W_MIN_WARNING_S)`. `TELL_MAX_TICKS` is fixed by Pillar 2's text ("10–30 seconds") and by Save/Load's `tell_remaining` range. The tunable draw bounds satisfy `TELL_MIN_TICKS ≤ TELL_DRAW_LO ≤ TELL_DRAW_HI ≤ TELL_MAX_TICKS` (lint). **Draw bounds (CQ-4, closed): `TELL_DRAW_LO` 900 and `TELL_DRAW_HI` 1800 `[PLACEHOLDER]`**, so a tell a player meets in play lasts 15 to 30 seconds, inside Pillar 2's 10 to 30; the full 600-tick floor is reachable only through `attention_arm_tell` (AT-21) and fixtures. A second lint, `abortability_play`, binds the played range: `t_decay(ring) + REACT_ALLOW_TICKS ≤ TELL_DRAW_LO − 6` at every ring (`REACT_ALLOW_TICKS` 180 `[PLACEHOLDER]`; it also runs the `x_dark_home_lit` and `autonomous_transient` rows, F-15b, AT-6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the R10 (b) invariant still binds at `TELL_MIN_TICKS` (AT-10). **Hard rule:** no path reaches BREACH before `tell_start_T + tell_len`, and `tell_len ≥ TELL_MIN_TICKS` on **every** path, including `attention_arm_tell` (AT-21). There is no "LOUD event → instant breach". Attention uses stream `"attention.tell"`; Horror keeps `"horror.tell"` for its own sub-tell (the kernel example is a refresh owed, C8). Rate-coupled length is a Vertical Slice playtest candidate.
*Criterion.* AC-AT-01a (written first), AC-AT-18, AC-AT-19, AC-AT-30, AC-AT-64, AC-AT-130 (the re-key). *Pillar.* P2. *Decided by:* R9; Pillar 2 design test; SL:528; user ruling D16 (OQ-AT-29).

**AT-9. Escalation: elapsed-keyed beats and tiers.** *Rule.* Escalation is keyed to the **escalation clock** `esc_ticks`, published as `tell_elapsed` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(user ruling OQ-AT-25, Option A)*: it is 0 on the TELL-entry run and then advances by 6 on every run whose integrated `L' ≥ theta_HOLD` and stays where it is on every run under the line (the same comparison that counts `below_hold_runs`, AT-10). It is **never** keyed to progress through `tell_len`: a progress-keyed cadence peaks exactly at the breach and leaks the end, whereas keyed to the player's own behaviour a 600-tick and an 1800-tick tell are identical for as long as the clock runs (the dread of not knowing), and nothing the clock carries depends on `tell_len` or `breach_due_T`. A player who stays loud sees the clock equal real elapsed time (`T − tell_start_T`) and the schedule below is the old elapsed-keyed one exactly; a player who goes under the hold line freezes the beat interval and the tier where they are, because the signal is earned: complying never makes the tell worse, and the escalation resumes only if the level climbs back to the line. The clock never runs backwards, so `tier` never falls inside an epoch. Beats keep publishing in real time at the frozen interval until the abort or the due run; only the interval and the tier freeze. Real elapsed time stays derivable as `T − phase_enter_T` and is not a hidden quantity. One SIM counter, `tell_beat`, drives **both** senses: each increment is one audio beat and one visual filament-resolve event in every lit region. Beat 0 is published in the TELL-entry run, so audio is first and the presenter may render no filament for an epoch before beat 0 exists (the art bible's rule that every tell has an audio component starting no later than its visual, HR-9). The beat interval shrinks from `BEAT_START_TICKS` (150) to `BEAT_END_TICKS` (45) over `BEAT_RAMP_TICKS` (1800) of the escalation clock, with jitter of ±`BEAT_JITTER_TICKS` (8) from a **pure integer hash** of `(tell_epoch, k, HASH_SEED)`, never from `rng_derive`, and each gap at least `BEAT_MIN_GAP_TICKS` (30). The schedule is built from nominal offsets, so run quantisation (a beat may publish up to five ticks late) never accumulates. `tier = 0` outside TELL and `1 + (e ≥ 600) + (e ≥ 1200)` inside, with `e = esc_ticks` (the whole floor window is tier 1 whatever the player does, because `esc_ticks` never exceeds real elapsed time), which is Lighting's tier-1 recipe (registry `gutter_recipe`: tier 1 480/960 frames, tier 2 from `TIER2_TICKS` 300/600, tier 3 from `TIER3_TICKS` 180/360, placeholders). Filament density in a lit region is a function of `tell_beat` (AV-7), which follows this schedule. **Two-channel criterion.** (auto, headless) every legal `(tell_len, seed)` and every legal level trajectory (including a clock frozen from the first run) publishes at least `MIN_BEATS_IN_FLOOR` (4) beats in `[tell_start_T, tell_start_T + TELL_MIN_TICKS)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; (manual, screenshot plus audio capture) the presenter renders each beat in both senses; the audio channel is sufficient alone, and the visual channel is sufficient alone while an eligible emitter is lit (ART:954) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The lamp gutter is an optional **third** channel: Lighting's tier-1 spacing (480/960 frames) can give zero dips inside the 600-tick floor window (C2), so the contract does not lean on it; the shorter tier-2/3 spacing asked for in OQ-AT-7 now exists in the registry `gutter_recipe` as placeholder bounds. Attention publishes *facts*; Adaptive Audio & Tells owns every sound, mix and cue name (its requests are in Visual/Audio Requirements and Interactions as must-repeat). **Final-gap beat suppression is dropped (CQ-5, closed):** `BEAT_MIN_GAP_TICKS` constrains consecutive beats only, with no beat-to-breach gap, so the worst case for an organic tell in the floor window is five beats (offsets 0, 158, 307, 448, 580) against `MIN_BEATS_IN_FLOOR` 4, and the universal bound over every level trajectory (the clock frozen from the first run) is exactly four (0, 158, 316, 474; F-12) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; `BEAT_START_TICKS` 135 is recorded only as the fallback if the suppression ever returns. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), OQ-AT-25: escalation freezes while `L < theta_HOLD` (behaviour-keyed, Option A; the creative-director's call under coordination rule 3).** It replaces the elapsed-keyed text above, keeps the end unreadable (the clock keys on the player's own restraint, never on `tell_len`), changes AT-9, F-12, F-13, the persisted fields and the Audio tier layering (Adaptive Audio's contrary recommendation to reject freezing, OQ-AA-34, is superseded), and redoes the F-12 floor proof. The Feel AC AC-AT-125 still measures the share of first-time testers who stay still and reopens the ruling if it fails *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
*Criterion.* AC-AT-20 to AC-AT-24, AC-AT-47, AC-AT-127 (the freeze), AC-AT-128 (the floor under any trajectory). *Pillar.* P2. *Decided by:* R11; ART:954, :980; user ruling OQ-AT-25.

**AT-10. Restraint aborts a tell.** *Rule.* During TELL, after each run's integration: if `L < theta_HOLD` then `below_hold_runs += 1`, else it resets to 0. The tell **aborts to CALM** when `below_hold_runs × 6 ≥ ABORT_HOLD_TICKS` (placeholder 120, run-quantised; the first run under the line counts as run 1), **or** at the first run with `T ≥ breach_due_T` if `L < theta_HOLD` at that run, **or** at that same run if the departure void holds (`locus_vacated`, AT-22; *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*). If both are true on the same run the abort wins (one transition). An abort deposits no STRESS, switches no beacon, sets `tell_outcome = ABORTED`, freezes `tell_beat`, leaves `L` unchanged (a knob `ABORT_RELIEF_PM` defaulting to 1000, which means "no relief" and means the abort is unchanged from the ruled behaviour, lets a tuner cap the level at an abort if playtests show chained-abort fatigue) and sets `rearm_until_T = T + TELL_REARM_TICKS` (placeholder 600). **The rearm keys on the item, not on the pickup** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*: while a TELL runs, Attention records in `tell_carry_items` (persisted, AT-1) the `carry_ref` of every seat whose `BURDEN` push it drained (an ordered read of `controller.state`, the same read as `loco_state`, AT-31); after an abort the set is kept until `rearm_until_T`. On any CALM run before `rearm_until_T` that drains a `BURDEN` push from a seat whose `carry_ref` is in the set, `rearm_until_T` is set to that run's `T`, so dropping the cargo to abort and taking the same item up again grants no fresh `TELL_REARM_TICKS` immunity: the next crossing opens a tell at once. A different item leaves the rearm in place. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* The test is the push, not the pickup: any CALM run before `rearm_until_T` that drains a `BURDEN` push from a seat whose `carry_ref` is in the set ends the rearm, whether the seat re-took the item or never put it down (a continuous hold). By the location gate of AT-3 the push is not drained `IN_POD` or aboard the home body, so a hauler who hops with the item is not charged here: the void sets `rearm_until_T = T_d + TELL_REARM_TICKS` (`T_d` the due run) and it holds through the pod leg and the home carry. The cancel can fire after a hop only if the seat is back aboard a non-home body still holding the item before `rearm_until_T`: that takes a round trip, 2 × (`HOP_LEG_TICKS` 900 + `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` 45) = 1,890 ticks from the hop, against a rearm that ends d + 600 ticks after the hop (d = ticks of the tell still to run at the hop), so it is reachable only when d > 1,890 − 600 = 1,290 (a hop in the first 510 ticks of an 1,800-tick tell); otherwise the rearm is whole. The narrower rule, that only a re-take cancels, is not adopted (creative-director lean). The set is cleared at TELL entry (and refilled during the tell), at BREACH entry (a breached tell sets no rearm) and when the rearm ends. A player who keeps being loud through the tell forfeits the abort; that is intended ("we chose to be loud"). Restraint always costs the partial (Formulas F-15b), and that price is deliberate *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; it is balanced by a breach that has teeth (AT-11), so neither choice dominates. `tell_remaining` published to Save/Load is the time to `breach_due_T`: the conservative direction, because an abort only ends the block early. Two invariants, both lint: **(a) rearm against autosave:** `TELL_REARM_TICKS ≥ AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS` (cited), which guarantees an open soft-gate window between chained aborted tells even under STRICT mode. **(b) abortability at entry:** a player who enters TELL at the highest possible level (`L_CEIL`, AT-5) and then zeroes every player-controlled input (still, beam off, no verbs, any cargo set down) falls under `theta_HOLD` minus a margin `ATT_MARGIN` before `TELL_MIN_TICKS − 6` ticks elapse, at the ring's survivable-dark floor. In words: the tell is a window of agency even at its shortest. The play-level variant, which adds a reaction allowance and evaluates against the shortest draw a player can actually meet, is the registered formula `abortability_play` (AT-8, CQ-4; Formulas F-15b).
*Criterion.* AC-AT-25, AC-AT-26, AC-AT-27, AC-AT-16, AC-AT-52. *Pillar.* P3 (restraint is real), P2 (a tell is a window of agency). *Decided by:* R10; Pillar 3 design test.

#### Group E — The breach and its locus

**AT-11. Breach entry actions (same run).** *Rule.* At the run that satisfies `T ≥ breach_due_T` with `L ≥ theta_HOLD`: `phase = BREACH`, `breach_enter_T = T`; record `locus_occupants_at_entry` = the set of living seats whose `actor_section` is in `locus_body` at this BREACH-entry run; M17 `deposit_trace(STRESS, s, magnitude = BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT)` for every section `s` of the locus body, in ascending `section_id`, at most `STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` (placeholder 8) per run, continuing on following runs (`stress_pending_cursor`) until the body is covered; and `set_beacon(on)` submitted as a `SYSTEM` command at T+1 (CR-9 path b). The magnitude is cited by registry name and never as a number; passing that constant as `magnitude` also makes the Graph's M17 clamp reading (`stress_pm = clamp(magnitude, 1000, 3000)`) and its D.9 / LS-25 reading (`stress_pm = BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT`) agree (C15, a Graph wording refresh). **Footprint cap:** `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` bounds honoured footprints per Graph run; Attention takes at most `STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN` per run. **Attention has no first claim on the cap** (CP-C5): Horror's footprints arrive by **path (a)**: the published Class B mutators `deposit_trace` (M17) and `apply_suit_damage`, called from the `horror.step` hook, which is ordered `after` Attention (KRN Interactions row 9; Horror HE-28, C-HE-3), not as SYSTEM commands in P2; Horror submits no SYSTEM command at MVP. The Graph's "first `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` in arrival order within P2" (LSG:807) carries a P2 premise that path (a) does not satisfy, so Attention claims no first place in the cap. The guarantee is therefore a **Horror must-repeat**: its per-run footprint budget is at most `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP − STRESS_DEPOSITS_PER_RUN`. The registry unit of `MAX_FOOTPRINTS_PER_STEP` (revised 2026-10-27) says per run across all callers and subjects (global), the first 16 by arrival applied in ascending subject id and the rest dropped and counted, which matches LSG:727 (C22). A STRESS deposit the cap drops is not lost for good: the next burst run re-arms it (AT-12; an edge case below). **Attention's MVP breach is STRESS plus the beacon plus the published phase.** RUPTURE and GOUGE are Horror's; this keeps Attention fully testable without Horror. **Stance (the breach is a consequence amplifier, stated so it is a decision):** STRESS multiplies *endogenous* damage only ("the breach rhythm makes the ship *fail* faster, not *leak* faster", LSG D.9), so a breach costs the crew what they had deferred; on a clean ship it would be nearly a non-event. **Why this is not left as a stance (gate ruling, CD-GDD-ALIGN, applied):** each choice is defensible alone, but a toothless breach on a clean ship together with an abort that always forfeits the partial (AT-10, Moment A) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* makes *commit* the dominant choice. Restraint would always cost the partial, riding it out would cost almost nothing, P3's "restraint and stealth are real strategies" would be empty, the "chaos" half of P2 would have no chaos, and players would learn to ignore tells. Two requirements follow, and neither is a mitigation to be traded away. **(1) Content requirement (a Derelict Authoring must-repeat).** Every body that can be a locus on MVP derelicts A and B is authored with at least one active overload or fatigue fault (on derelict A, a fault that wakes when its bus is served: option (b), OQ-AT-24), so a derelict breach always has something to amplify (AC-AT-58 is the seeded-fault scenario, AC-AT-117 the authoring check). This fits P5: the outer ring is kept unsafe by wear. A body the player has repaired clean is the player's earned result and not a content failure, and a home-ship locus carries whatever the crew has left unrepaired. **(2) Horror Entities' single MVP behaviour wired to BREACH is a BLOCKING dependency** (OQ-AT-9, AC-AT-77), no longer an ask: a breach brings the thing the crew fears, not only a faster-failing hull. `BREACH_PROPAGATION_MULT` is not raised to hide this. **Playtest tripwire:** the Moment-ordering guard (Player Fantasy, AC-AT-80) is named for exactly this failure: a 30-minute session with only breaches means commit has become dominant. **Re-evaluated against the designed Horror and Derelict Authoring** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the claim that STRESS alone leaves a derelict breach toothless was written before Horror existed. Horror now supplies crew-side teeth of its own: by HE-F16 a stationary seat in the locus body cannot be killed in a minimum-length breach (`BREACH_MIN_TICKS` 900 gives two REACH starts) but can be in any breach of at least 986 ticks and certainly in any of at least 1,156, and the REACH ladder (HE-F13, HE-F17) gives the breach a content beat. The breach therefore has two teeth: STRESS (ship-side, it amplifies deferred faults) and Horror's REACH (crew-side, it needs a seat that lingers); neither substitutes for the other, and a crew that leaves the body by pod is exposed to neither beyond the STRESS tail. Requirement (1) stays as the ship-side tooth. **Derelict A, option (b)** (creative-director recommendation; **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), OQ-AT-24: option (b)**, which preserves EM-24's count of 8 live faults; the dead-bus exemption (a) is not adopted) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: its pass condition is a Graph subject authored with a fault that *wakes when its bus is served* (`j_a_main`, a dead SHORT that becomes live once fed, with `pump_a` on its branch), which keeps Emitter State's count of exactly 8 live faults (EM-24) and adds no ninth fault. **Story-readiness gate:** a story that builds AT-11, the breach ACs or Derelict Authoring's locus lint is not ready until AC-AT-58's tolerance is fixed with the Graph owner (OQ-AT-6); OQ-AT-24 is answered (user ruling, option (b)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
*Criterion.* AC-AT-28, AC-AT-29, AC-AT-30, AC-AT-58 (seeded-fault scenario). *Pillar.* P2, P3. *Decided by:* R12; LSG:196, :525, :906.

**AT-12. Breach duration and end.** *Rule.* During BREACH the level **keeps integrating** (the player's noise still matters), with `W_L[FAULT_GLOW] = W_L[BEACON] = 0` and the beacon's lamp watts never reaching the power terms (`bcn_main` is a LAMP node, so it sits inside `lamps_lit_w`, AT-4; the alarm cannot hold the level above `theta_HOLD` and delay the exit it is tested against) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. STRESS is re-armed in **bursts**: `STRESS_REFRESH_BURST_RUNS` (3) consecutive runs every `STRESS_REFRESH_RUNS` (placeholder 300) runs, under the lint `STRESS_REFRESH_RUNS + STRESS_REFRESH_BURST_RUNS < STRESS_HOLD_STEPS` (cited from LSG:907; registry `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS`). A burst tolerates one dropped deposit because a deposit is idempotent. BREACH ends at the first of: (i) `BREACH_MAX_TICKS` (placeholder 3600, the death-spiral guard); (ii) after `BREACH_MIN_TICKS` (placeholder 900), `L < theta_HOLD` for `CLEAR_HOLD_TICKS` (placeholder 300, run-quantised); (iii) pod-hop departure: the last living occupant recorded at BREACH entry (`locus_occupants_at_entry`) leaving a locus body that is not the home-ship (AT-22); (iv) **ADDITION X10 (APPROVED at the CD-GDD-ALIGN gate: the combat anti-pillar explicitly permits decoys, and the lit derelict pays in STRESS on its own hardware; CR-LURE stays a playtest watch item with `LOCUS_OCC_PREF_PM` as the lever):** if at BREACH entry the locus body is not the home-ship and `locus_occupants_at_entry` is empty (it holds no living player), at `BREACH_MIN_TICKS` (the retreat the departure clause models has already happened) (reachable at MVP only through a derelict that Web Map keeps loaded while berthed, WM-21 and WM-24, after the player has left it; a *departed* unberthed derelict goes dormant at once under LS-17's default, which Web Map adopts, so that form is fixture-only *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*). **Breach length is Attention's, not `STRESS_HOLD_STEPS`.** STRESS lapses on the Graph's own hold after the last deposit and may outlast SUBSIDING: "a long tell, a spreading wrongness, a short collapse, then silence" (LSG:986). No Attention surface shows that tail. **Must-repeat request to Adaptive Audio & Tells (R30):** `phase == CALM` is never mapped to an "all clear" cue, because the Graph's consequence sounds, not Attention, carry the ongoing wrongness; this is Audio's rule to repeat, not Attention's.
*Criterion.* AC-AT-31, AC-AT-32, AC-AT-33 (lint), AC-AT-34. *Pillar.* P2, P3. *Decided by:* R12.

**AT-13. Subsiding and the refractory.** *Rule.* On SUBSIDING entry: `set_beacon(off)` is submitted; no further STRESS deposits are made; and the level is reset to a residual, not wiped: `L ← min(L, B + POST_PM × (theta − B) / 1000)` with `POST_PM` a placeholder of 400. SUBSIDING lasts `SUBSIDE_TICKS` (placeholder 1200) while integrating normally, then the machine returns to CALM with `refract_until_T = T + REFRACT_TICKS` (placeholder 1800) and `tell_outcome = BREACHED`. During the refractory no TELL may begin, but the level keeps integrating, so **the refractory is not free safe time**: a player still loud at its end tips straight into a new tell (bounded by `L_CEIL`). The refractory is a published, state-gated valley, not a hidden scheduler. `phase` changes only inside `attention.step`; `post_restore` changes no phase and submits nothing (AT-27), so no reader can observe a half state; CALM → BREACH, TELL → SUBSIDING and BREACH → TELL do not exist. The phase table, guards and who may cause each transition are in States and Transitions.
*Criterion.* AC-AT-35, AC-AT-36, AC-AT-60 (table-driven transition test). *Pillar.* P2. *Decided by:* R13; LSG:986.

**AT-14. Locus and locus body.** *Rule.* The **locus** is the section with the highest `ledger_mAU` at TELL entry; ties go to the lowest `section_id`. It is fixed for the epoch and falls back to the home-ship's lowest `section_id` only if the locus section is cut away or goes dormant *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* and no departure void applies: the fallback never converts an escape into a breach on the ship the player escaped to (AT-22, E-23). **During a TELL the dormancy fallback is suppressed from the first run at which `locus_vacated` holds** (a non-home locus body, `tell_occupants_at_entry` non-empty, no living seat in `locus_body`): the departure apply makes the derelict dormant many runs before `breach_due_T`, and without this the fallback would re-point the locus at the home ship in between and the due-run void would then never see the recorded body. The locus stays pinned to the departed body for the epoch (`locus_section_id` and `locus_body` remain valid ids; its ledger entry is dropped per AT-2, which is harmless because the locus is fixed), and the void resolves at the due run. The fallback is taken during a TELL only for a cut, a berth release, or a dormancy with a living seat still in the body. Attribution: a PlayerId source maps to the section containing the actor's foot origin through Ship Body's `actor_section(actor_id)` (BDY-29, Section lookup for Suit; sibling in flight); an object or emitter source maps to `section_of` or the emitter's `section_id`; light and power map to their own section. The **locus body** is `sections_of(body_of(locus))` (Layout reads, LY state inventory and Body row), recorded at TELL entry as `locus_body`. STRESS covers the whole locus body: welded sections share the breach, so a welded derelict is not a safe harbour. An optional knob `LOCUS_OCC_PREF_PM` (default 1000 = "leader only", conforming) lets a tuner prefer a section holding a living player if playtests show an unattended, powered derelict absorbing most breaches. Layout's pathing asks (`room_surface`, `floor_tile_at`, `room_adjacency`, LY Interactions row for Attention / Horror) are Horror's; Attention takes only the membership reads.
*Criterion.* AC-AT-37, AC-AT-59 (decoy knob default reproduces the rule). *Pillar.* P3. *Decided by:* R14.

#### Group F — The contract, the view, the truth channel

**AT-15. The tell-window contract: one predicate for all web-originated harm.** *Rule.* `exogenous_permitted(section) = phase ∈ {BREACH, SUBSIDING} AND section ∈ locus_body`. Every web-originated exogenous call (M17 RUPTURE, GOUGE and STRESS; environmental M18 `apply_damage(..., EXOGENOUS)`) must satisfy it. The bed is what makes a tell on an unoccupied lit derelict fair. Player-originated exogenous acts (cut, vent) never need the tell (LSG:144: agency); the Graph's endogenous gate (`W_MIN_WARNING_S`) is not how this contract is enforced and neither replaces nor is replaced by it. **This rule discharges LSG:1063** ("every call site of M17 RUPTURE, GOUGE and STRESS and every environmental M18 `apply_damage(…, EXOGENOUS)` source is preceded by that system's own 10–30 s Pillar 2 tell, named in its GDD, and none relies on the Graph's gate for it").
*Criterion.* AC-AT-01 (first; discharges LSG:1063), AC-AT-01a, AC-AT-68 (the provisional crew-body scope). *Pillar.* P2. *Decided by:* R15; LSG:144, :1063.

**AT-16. The published read view.** *Rule.* `attention.view` is a SIM read view of integers, never `PERCEPTION_OUT` (AC-SL-95a, AC-SL-121). The field set is final (Save/Load and Audio restate these names):

| Field | Values | Reader and note |
|---|---|---|
| `phase` | CALM, TELL, BREACH, SUBSIDING | Audio, Lighting, Presenter, Sanity, Horror. **Audio reads `phase`, never `breach_phase`** (lint) |
| `breach_phase` | CALM, BREACH, SUBSIDING | **Save/Load only.** TELL is reported as CALM so Save/Load's FAIR mode stays live (C5); not an edit to Save/Load |
| `tell_active` | 0/1 | Save/Load |
| `tell_remaining` | 0 to `TELL_MAX_TICKS`, 0 outside TELL | Save/Load, SIM readers (Horror) and the DIAGNOSTIC Debug Overlay only; **never a PRESENTATION subscriber** |
| `tell_elapsed` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | 0 to `TELL_MAX_TICKS`, 0 outside TELL; **the escalation clock** (`esc_ticks`, AT-9): equal to real elapsed time while the level stays at or above `theta_HOLD`, frozen while it is under; real elapsed time is `T − phase_enter_T` | Audio, Presenter, Lighting (readers that scale intensity or schedule tiers key on this or on `tier`, never on a clock of their own) |
| `tell_beat`, `tell_beat_T` | counter, tick | Audio, Presenter |
| `tier` | 0 to 3 | Lighting (`tier ≥ 1`), Audio, Sanity |
| `tell_outcome` | NONE, ABORTED, BREACHED | Audio, Sanity; NONE until the first tell ends, ABORTED from an abort until the next TELL entry, BREACHED from SUBSIDING end until the next TELL entry; survives load |
| `tell_epoch` | int, +1 at every TELL entry | all (replaces the brief's `breach_epoch`, because aborted tells have no breach) |
| `phase_enter_T`, `breach_enter_T` | ticks | Audio, Presenter |
| `level_pm` | 0 to 1000, baseline-relative: `min(1000, ⌊1000 × (L − B) / (theta − B)⌋)` | Presenter and Audio, **quantised only** (AT-26) |
| `locus_section_id` | id | Audio, Horror |
| `exogenous_permitted(section)` | predicate | Horror, Graph-side callers |

`tell_progress_pm` is **not published** (it would leak the end). Audio's dedupe key is the pair `(tell_epoch, tell_beat)` compared lexicographically, because a new tell resets `tell_beat` to 0 while `tell_epoch` increases. Published-field table by phase is in States and Transitions. The Save/Load gate formula (`attention_tell_block`, `soft_block`) is owned by Save/Load; Attention owns only the three field *values* and their names. **The read view of Save/Load's SL-5 Soft (b) (answers Save/Load OQ-24):** the condition reads `attention.view` (SIM), and nothing else of Attention: the active tell is `tell_active` = 1, its remaining ticks are `tell_remaining` (compared by Save/Load against `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` under `gate_tell_mode` FAIR; STRICT defers for the whole tell), and the breach phase is `breach_phase` (CALM, BREACH, SUBSIDING; TELL reports CALM, C5). **Pod-hop notification:** the name is Web Map & Transit's, not Attention's; Web Map WM-31 names `POD_DEPARTED` and `POD_ARRIVED` (names provisional until its registry merge), and `POD_ARRIVED` is the one it lists Save/Load as consuming as an event trigger. Attention needs neither for correctness (AT-22 derives departure from Ship Body).
*Criterion.* AC-AT-38, AC-AT-39, AC-AT-40, AC-AT-66, AC-AT-67, AC-SL-121 (discharged). *Pillar.* P1, P2. *Decided by:* R16; SL:517, :528, :531.

**AT-17. The tell is a truth channel.** *Rule.* Nothing Attention publishes or presents is removed, added, delayed or altered by the Perception Filter or by Sanity. There is **no phantom tell and no false calm, in any tier and at any stage** (gate ruling, CD-GDD-ALIGN: rejected by pillar, permanent, not deferred): a false calm hides a real tell and produces exactly the ambush Pillar 2 forbids, and a phantom tell spends the player's restraint on a lie and voids `TellAudit`. The tell is a standing truth channel in every tier; Sanity keeps its own disjoint sound family and its own rim fringe (AV-17). The art bible's tell element "a needle that drifts on a *real* gauge" (ART 2.7) is **dropped from the tell (C1)**: no Graph or instrument value may take Attention as input (LSG:281), and a gauge moving with no physical cause would be a lie that Failure & Trail refuses to draw (FT-4); a real needle change caused by breach STRESS damage is a breach *consequence*, not a tell, and the wording amendment is routed to the art-director and In-World Instruments. Attention reads no sanity and no `PERCEPTION_OUT` value (CR-12).
*Criterion.* AC-AT-41, AC-AT-40. *Pillar.* P4, P1. *Decided by:* R17.

#### Group G — The world writes and the presenter

**AT-18. The beacon.** *Rule.* BEACON `gates_actions` is **false**: Attention concurred (the beacon sweeps the cone over a point for roughly a tenth of each sweep) and the user has ruled (Emitter D20, confirmed 2026-10-27, OQ-AT-2 resolved) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the registry's "provisional, user decision pending" mark on `emitter_kind` is cleared by the registry request, not here. The Emitter State's `set_beacon` `max_age_ticks` of **120 is confirmed by Attention** (EM asks for exactly that): a T+1 SYSTEM command with 20 runs of slack. **Which beacon:** per Derelict Authoring DA-24 *(`derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md`, status Designed since 2026-10-27; was In Design at authoring)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, exactly one BEACON exists in the world, on `home_ship` in `spine_corridor`, authored with `node_ref` = `bcn_main`, a dedicated LOAD node (`mod_lamp`, 20 W, DA-24; OQ-DA-9 closed 'no sharing') under the lint `BEACON_COUNT` (ERROR, BOOT); derelicts A and B have none. DA-24 adds "Attention … may relocate it": **placement is Authoring's data row and is not Attention's** (refresh owed to DA, C20); Attention only submits `set_beacon` to the one beacon the data holds. Attention switches that beacon on at **every** BREACH entry regardless of locus, because it asserts a true global fact ("a breach is on"); the positional creak layer (AUD-4 a, in TELL) and STRESS carry *where*; *that* is carried by the beacon where it is in view and by Audio's alarm pulse on its aligned or fallback clock (the non-positional tell bed ended at BREACH entry, Audio AA-20) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. It switches off at SUBSIDING entry. `W_L[BEACON] = 0`. **The beacon is also a Graph LOAD** (its own LOAD node `bcn_main`, 20 W, DA-24), so switching it on adds draw and a `delta_w_last5` step on the home-ship. Attention needs no beacon-specific term *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: LS-19 defines `lamps_lit_w` as including any LAMP node such as `bcn_main`, so the beacon's 20 W draw and its switch-on step are inside the lamp subset that F-4 already removes, and the alarm cannot feed the level that the BREACH exit tests (C11 closed). `fx_cryo_lamp` (DA-23) is the one `node_ref` 0 fixture and is never touched by the tell. Under reduced flashing the beacon becomes a static mark (LO-26). LO-26 also names a HUD glyph, which contradicts ART:741 and is routed as C27, so the static mark and the audio carry the breach. A rejected `set_beacon` (`NOT_LIVE` when home-ship power is dead, `NO_SUCH_EMITTER`, `NOT_BEACON`) is logged once and retried once per run for `BEACON_RETRY_RUNS` (placeholder 20, equal to the command's max age); it never blocks the machine. Alarm cadence (one pulse per `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS`) is a must-repeat request to Adaptive Audio, not an Attention rule.
*Criterion.* AC-AT-42, AC-AT-29, AC-AT-63 (the beacon never reaches the power terms). *Pillar.* P2. *Decided by:* R18; EM:165, :200.

**AT-19. The suppressant: contract only.** *Rule.* The contract is stated and **no effect verb ships at MVP**: Attention reads `tool_charge(player_id, def_id)` (0..`charges_max`; `def_id` = `tool_suppressant`) through an ordered read and is never pushed to by Suit; the verb's registrant calls `consume_charge(player_id, def_id) -> ok`; and `OUT_OF_CHARGES` is the repeated read name (SE-14 and its open question 7, ruled CK-5). Answer to IDB OQ-16: at MVP the suppressant has no Attention effect, full or empty; any MVP effect is Horror Entities' (repel or distract, never touching the level or a tell). Horror ships none (HE-39). **Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), X6 Option A (Attention OQ-AT-5, Horror OQ 3, Suit OQ-34, Item DB OQ 29):** `tool_suppressant` is **removed from the MVP start kit** (Suit SE-11 slot 4, SE-14, SE-15, the Item DB MVP list and the HUD), so no inert tool reaches the player; HE-39 repel stays a dormant `[CUT-FIRST]` interface, AC-HE-124 is BLOCKING and IDB AC-109 passes. This document cites no `SUPPRESSANT_START_CHARGES` value (the registry retirement belongs to Suit and the Item DB) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The contract names above stand for the Vertical Slice addendum, and Attention declares `after: suit.vitals` only if a future revision reads Suit state (none at MVP).
*Criterion.* AC-AT-43. *Pillar.* P3. *Decided by:* R19; IA:133, SE:201, IDB:249.

**AT-20. The Attention Presenter (the world tells).** *Rule.* A PRESENTATION subscriber owned by this GDD draws, at MVP: (a) rim **filaments only inside a lit region of a player-controllable real emitter** (the gate widening, below; unlit space draws none: Principle 1, ART:302), and (b) a **dust-direction change in the beam**. **Hull-stress hairlines are cut from MVP** and routed to the art-director: they read too easily as the Integrity trail (ART:312, :565) and risk Pillar 1. Filaments are web pieces in the Y-sort layer (rotation permitted for web and horror pieces, PIPE row 16); colour is the web's iridescence only (teal → green → bronze → gold, ART:1371), never flesh or violet. The camera does nothing (PIPE:151); the beam, ambient light, camera and controls do not change in any phase (ART 2.7, PCI:135). **"Lit region" (gate ruling CD-GDD-ALIGN, OQ-AT-3 closed).** A strand resolves at the edge of the lit region of a **player-controllable real emitter**: the eligible kinds are exactly `BEAM` (the cone), `FIXTURE`, `NODE_LANTERN` and `DEPLOYABLE` (a pool, with a rim band of `RIM_BAND_PM` of the emitter's reach), the kinds of the registry's closed `emitter_kind` list that the player can switch, power, carry or place. **Excluded:** `BEACON` (the alarm lens is not a tell carrier), the cryo EMERGENCY lamp `fx_cryo_lamp` (FIXTURE subkind EMERGENCY, self-powered; keeps LO-20, "never a tell carrier"), `FAULT_GLOW` (a latent fault's glow is a consequence, not a tell) and the **DOCK_STATUS** glow of the berthed pod's dock room (FIXTURE subkind DOCK_STATUS, X2: self-powered and switched by SYSTEM only, so not a player-controllable emitter; it is light and an unswitchable one, AT-6, but a site lit only by it is not eligible) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. In co-op, filaments resolve in every lit region, each beat shared (SHARED_SUMMARY).
*Criterion.* AC-AT-44, AC-AT-45, AC-AT-53. *Pillar.* P3, P1. *Decided by:* R20; PIPE:305.

#### Group H — Seams, determinism, scope

**AT-21. The arming seam (test and onboarding).** *Rule.* `attention_arm_tell {tell_len}` has `allowed_origins {SYSTEM}`, no player binding and no PLAYER origin. It is valid only in CALM (otherwise rejected `NOT_CALM`); `tell_len` is clamped to `[TELL_MIN_TICKS, TELL_MAX_TICKS]`; the tell then follows every rule of AT-8 to AT-13.
